chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever removes a harmful obstruction from the path of Makkah, Allah writes for him a good deed; and whoever is written for him a good deed, He does not punish him.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for removing obstacles from the path of Makkah?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the spiritual merit of clearing physical impediments from the route to Makkah, linking it directly to divine mercy. This act of removing 'adh' (nuisance or harm) is presented not merely as civic duty but as a specific mechanism for securing forgiveness and averting punishment, reflecting the Shia emphasis on practical piety in daily life. The chain of narration underscores the reliability of this teaching within the Usuli tradition.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Yahya Bin Al Mubarak, from Abdullah Bin Jabala, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The one who removes a harmful obstruction from a stree of Makkah, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Write for him a good deed; and the one for whom a good deed is Written, He<sup>azwj</sup> would not Punish him’.
en.sarwar: 34. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Yahya’ ibn al-Mubarak from ‘Abd Allah ibn Jabalah from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ‘
If one removes something causing hardships to people on the way to Makkah, Allah writes down for him one good deed and one for whom a good deed is written, he is not subjected to punishment.’”
